subject: Post-call: Confirm data scope, residency, and break-glass flow for FinMate
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@finmate.com>
Cc: Neha Reddy <neha.reddy@finmate.com>
Date: 2026-06-14T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Confirm data scope, residency, and break-glass flow for FinMate

Hi Sam / Neha —

Thanks again for the quick call earlier. Short recap + open items so we have alignment and can move toward procurement. I tried to keep this focused around the privacy & access items you highlighted.

Recap (what we heard)
- Data types that will flow to Redwood: customer-facing chat transcripts, account IDs (internal), email address, anonymized transaction metadata. No SSNs or full PANs are expected to be sent to the model.
- Residency: primary deployment preference is us-east-1 (US only).
- Retention: you want customer transcripts retained for <= 90 days; operational logs (auth, access) retained 12 months; long-term analytics exports are off by default.
- Support access: must be role-based, least-privilege, JIT for break-glass; every support session must be logged and approved by your SOC admin.

Open questions / confirmation items for Redwood (action items)
1) PII types confirmation: We need a single-line confirmation that FinMate will not send raw SSNs or PANs into production requests. We can accept tokenized/hashed identifiers — please confirm.
2) KMS / encryption: Do you require customer-managed KMS? If yes, we'll share integration notes and a short ops checklist.
3) Break-glass approvals: Who is your SOC approver for emergency access requests? Please provide name + email so we can populate the RBAC policy template.
4) Retention policy: Are the 90d transcript / 12mo logs fixed or do you want options to shorten retention for certain project IDs?

What Redwood will provide (by next week)
- Short SOC2 summary (attached) and a one-page support access playbook.
- RBAC snippet + example IAM roles for Break-glass and Support-Readonly.
- A mutual action plan (M.A.P.) draft with milestones for security review and procurement.

Next steps / owners
- Tessa (me): follow up with SOC2 summary and support playbook by EOD Tue (2026-06-15).
- Ben: draft RBAC role templates and example policies (target Wed).
- FinMate: confirm SOC approver + PII restrictions and KMS preference.

Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (high-level), support-access-playbook-v1.md (playbook stub)

Thanks — if I missed anything from the call, flag it and I will update.

Regards,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
T: +1 415-555-0199
From: Sam Lee <sam.lee@finmate.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Reddy <neha.reddy@finmate.com>, FinMate Procurement <procurement@finmate.com>
Date: 2026-06-14T16:11:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Confirm data scope, residency, and break-glass flow for FinMate

Tessa — thanks for the clear recap. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

1) PII: Confirmed — we will not send SSNs or PANs into production calls. We do use a hashed customer_id (SHA256) in some payloads; that is acceptable.
2) KMS: Procurement prefers customer-managed KMS for at-rest encryption. We’ll need a short integration checklist and an estimate of any impact to SLAs.
3) Break-glass: Our SOC approver is Neha Reddy (neha.reddy@finmate.com). Break-glass requests should route to her + our on-call SRE. We expect an audit trail + automatic revocation after 4 hours unless renewed.
4) Retention: 90d transcripts is fine for primary flows; we may request shorter retention for test environments.

Also — procurement requests a security artifact pack (SOC2 summary, encryption details, SOC contacts) to attach to the purchase order. Can you include that?

Thanks,
Sam
Director, Platform Security — FinMate
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-14T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: Confirm data scope, residency, and break-glass flow for FinMate

Team — forwarding FinMate replies. Short tasking so we can get this into the M.A.P. and procurement package.

Requirements from FinMate (explicit):
- CMK KMS required (customer-managed). Need integration steps and any SLA notes.
- Break-glass approval to Neha Reddy + on-call SRE; auto-revoke after 4h by default.
- Confirmed no SSNs/PANs; hashed customer_id is used.
- 90d transcripts; shorter retention for test environments optional.

Action items (owners + deadlines)
- Ben: produce RBAC role templates (Support-JIT, Support-ReadOnly, BreakGlass-Temp) + a short JIT request flow diagram. Deliverable: roles + policy snippets. Due: 2026-06-17 EOD.
- Marissa: assemble procurement security pack (SOC2 summary, encryption details, KMS integration checklist). Use the attached SOC2 summary as base and add KMS ops steps. Due: 2026-06-16 noon.
- Vivek: confirm whether CMK integration will have any performance/latency impact and draft guidance for ops (if any). Due: 2026-06-18.
- Tessa: draft MAP and send to FinMate for sign-off. Due: 2026-06-17.

Notes on implementation constraints I ran into on the call: we can support CMK but need the customer's key policy to allow Redwood service principal; we'll document the exact policy snippet in the KMS checklist. Break-glass will be implemented via JIT access: request -> owner's approval (Neha) -> short-lived role issuance (4 hours), all events logged to audit channel.

Pls ack and I'll follow up with docs attached.

—Tessa
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call: Confirm data scope, residency, and break-glass flow for FinMate

Got it — I’ll take RBAC. Plan:
- Draft role JSON + example STS/JIT issuance flow today.
- Include audit event examples (what fields we log, retention).
- Will flag any technical blockers after a quick config test against a dummy CMK.

Marking deliverable for 6/17 EOD.

Ben
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
